Filing Party                             Signer (Representative)                  Other Contact (Principal)

Basis for Intervening:
Pursuant to Rule 214 of the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission’s (“Commission” or “FERC”) Rules of Practice and Procedure, 18 C.F.R. § 385.214, the Ohio Environmental Council (“OEC”) respectfully moves to intervene in Docket No. ER27-126-000.
The Ohio Environmental Council (“OEC”) is an Ohio non-profit organization dedicated to safeguarding the health and environment of every Ohio community via legal advocacy, policy initiatives, civic engagement, and accountability for decision-makers. To advance equitable access to clean air, safe water, and a healthy environment, OEC actively engages in state and federal regulatory proceedings—including matters before FERC, the Ohio Power Siting Board and the Public Utilities Commission of Ohio—to promote clean, dependable, and affordable energy options. This activity includes intervention and participation in the Ohio Power Siting Board proceedings involving the facilities encompassing the “Flagship Project”  at the center of this proceeding. OEC’s distinct interests in this proceeding are not adequately represented by any other party, and its involvement directly serves the public interest. 

This proceeding concerns the executed "Study Agreement in Furtherance of the State of Ohio's State Agreement Approach Request," designated as Rate Schedule No. 54, filed by PJM Interconnection, L.L.C. (“PJM”). Under this Study Agreement, PJM will evaluate, on an integrated basis, the transmission infrastructure required to accommodate the “Flagship Project” centered at and around the former United States Department of Energy (“DOE”) Portsmouth Gaseous Diffusion Plant in Pike County, Ohio. The unprecedented scale of the Flagship Project involves an expansion of approximately 9,570 MW of artificial intelligence (“AI”) data center load (totaling 10,370 MW campus-wide), 10,170 MW of gross new generation—largely gas-fired—and three proposed new 765 kV transmission lines along with associated facilities.

The outcome of this proceeding directly implicates OEC’s mission and the vital Environmental, public health impacts and ratepayer and economic protection interests of its members and supporters in Pike County, neighboring communities, and across Ohio. Specifically, the cumulative impact of deploying over 10 GW of new gas-fired generation carries substantial environmental consequences, notably significant air emissions, greenhouse gas additions affecting climate goals, and severe strain on local ecosystems and watersheds. OEC is intervening to ensure that these environmental and public health impacts are comprehensively evaluated, and to safeguard local communities from compounding historic environmental injustices in the region. OEC is further committed to securing not only clean energy, but affordable, efficient, and reliable energy for Ohio residents. Because this proceeding initiates the State Agreement Approach to plan transmission solutions for this massive load and generation development, OEC intervenes to ensure that captive Ohio ratepayers and consumers are shielded from bearing inappropriate financial burdens, unjust cost-allocations, or grid reliability risks associated with the project's transmission and interconnection infrastructure.

OEC’s interest in this proceeding is not adequately represented by any other existing party, and its participation will contribute to a complete record and is firmly in the public interest pursuant to 18 C.F.R. § 385.214(b)(2)(iii). For the foregoing reasons, OEC respectfully requests that the Commission grant this Motion to Intervene and accord OEC full party status in this docket.
